body.statement:
For \(\ell=3\), \(r_\beta(3)=4\).  There is a Zariski-dense relatively Euclidean-open subset \(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal O_{3,3}\) such that every \(\zeta\in\mathcal S\) has at least one preimage \(\theta\in\Theta_{3,3}\) satisfying
\[
 \operatorname{rank}D(\Phi_{3,3},\beta)(\theta)=17
 >16=\operatorname{rank}D\Phi_{3,3}(\theta),
\]
and \(F_{3,3}(\zeta)\) contains a real legal curve along which \(\beta\) varies.  At order four, \(\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{id}}_{3,4}\ne\varnothing\), and the union of its domains \(\mathcal U_\chi\cap\mathcal O_{3,4}\) contains a nonempty relatively Zariski-open subset; every covering chart returns the common legal-fiber effect, while outside all chart domains every recovery map returns \(\bot\).  Consequently the three-latent workflow may replace \(C_{\le k(3)}=C_{\le7}\) by \(C_{\le4}\) on the regular legal image, whereas \(C_{\le3}\) does not generically identify a point effect on \(\mathcal S\).
body.justification: The exact three-latent case converts a fiber calculation into a seven-to-four reduction in required empirical cumulant order and a sharp order-three nonidentification decision.
body.gap: Tramontano et al., Theorems 3.4--3.5, specialize to the sufficient order \(k(3)=7\) and do not show either order-four sufficiency from the complete tensor or generic failure at order three.
body.consumer: For \(\ell=3\), CEId-from-Moments can stop after estimating \(C_{\le4}\) instead of \(C_{\le7}\); if only \(C_{\le3}\) is available on the open lower-fiber locus, it must return nonidentification rather than a selected point estimate.
body.proof_tex:
Order the twenty coordinates by
\[
 \vartheta=(\beta,\gamma,u_1,v_1,u_2,v_2,u_3,v_3,
 \kappa_{0,2},\kappa_{1,2},\kappa_{2,2},\kappa_{3,2},\kappa_{t,2},\kappa_{y,2},
 \kappa_{0,3},\kappa_{1,3},\kappa_{2,3},\kappa_{3,3},\kappa_{t,3},\kappa_{y,3}).
\]
Order the six quadratic tensor rows by
\[
 (2,0,0),(1,1,0),(1,0,1),(0,2,0),(0,1,1),(0,0,2)
\]
and the ten cubic rows lexicographically as
\[
\begin{gathered}
 (3,0,0),(2,1,0),(2,0,1),(1,2,0),(1,1,1),\\
 (1,0,2),(0,3,0),(0,2,1),(0,1,2),(0,0,3).
\end{gathered}
\]
At the rational point
\[
 \vartheta_i=\frac{(i+2)(i+3)}{i+1},\qquad 0\le i\le19,
\]
direct differentiation of the polynomial formula in Definition \(\mathrm{def:cumulant\mbox{-}map}\) gives, for the first sixteen parameter columns,
\[
 \det D\Phi_{3,3}[1{:}16]
 =\frac{5792045575840772656442004338637801362}{49633171875}\ne0.
\]
Appending the row \(D\beta=(1,0,\ldots,0)\) and taking the first seventeen columns gives
\[
 \det D(\Phi_{3,3},\beta)[1{:}17]
 =-\frac{19906139921937009119415063593996}{268019128125}\ne0.
\]
These displayed rational determinants are exact certificates for ranks sixteen and seventeen, respectively.

The point is legal.  Its six order-two source cumulants are positive.  Given any pair \((\kappa_2,\kappa_3)\) with \(\kappa_2>0\), put \(\delta=\kappa_3/\kappa_2\) and choose the unique \(A,B>0\) satisfying \(AB=\kappa_2\) and \(B-A=\delta\).  The centered two-point law with probabilities \(B/(A+B)\) at \(-A\) and \(A/(A+B)\) at \(B\) has variance \(AB=\kappa_2\) and third cumulant \(AB(B-A)=\kappa_3\).  It is finite, nondegenerate, and non-Gaussian.  Taking the six sources independently realizes the specified cumulants.  At the displayed structural point \(\beta=\gamma=6\), and
\[
 (u_1,u_2,u_3)=\left(\frac{20}{3},\frac{42}{5},\frac{72}{7}\right),
 \qquad
 (v_1,v_2,v_3)=\left(\frac{15}{2},\frac{28}{3},\frac{45}{4}\right),
\]
so every \(u_i-\gamma\) and \(v_i-\beta u_i\) is nonzero.  Thus the point lies in \(\Theta_{3,3}\).

For completeness, the rank certificate yields an actual legal fiber curve as follows.  Split \(\vartheta=(x,z)\), with \(x\) the first sixteen coordinates and \(z\) the remaining four.  The first determinant says that \(D_x\Phi_{3,3}\) is invertible.  For \((c,z)\) near \((c_0,z_0)=(\Phi_{3,3}(\vartheta_0),z_0)\), consider
\[
 \mathcal T_{c,z}(x)=x-\bigl[D_x\Phi_{3,3}(\vartheta_0)\bigr]^{-1}
       \{\Phi_{3,3}(x,z)-c\}.
\]
On a sufficiently small closed ball, continuity of the derivative makes \(\mathcal T_{c,z}\) a contraction mapping the ball into itself.  Its iterates are Cauchy because successive differences are bounded by a geometric series; completeness of the ball gives a unique fixed point \(x=h(c,z)\).  Differentiating the fixed-point equation gives
\[
 D_zh=-(D_x\Phi_{3,3})^{-1}D_z\Phi_{3,3}.
\]
The augmented rank-seventeen determinant is exactly the assertion that
\[
 D_z\{\beta(h(c_0,z),z)\}\ne0.
\]
Choosing a direction on which this derivative is nonzero and taking \(z(t)=z_0+ta\) gives a fiber curve \((h(c_0,z(t)),z(t))\) with nonconstant \(\beta\).  All strict moment and graph inequalities persist for sufficiently small \(t\).

Both determinants remain nonzero in a neighborhood.  The same fixed-point construction, now allowing \(c\) to vary and holding \(z=z_0\), shows that every \(c\) in an ambient Euclidean neighborhood \(\mathcal S\) of \(c_0\) has a legal preimage at which the two ranks are sixteen and seventeen.  Repeating the preceding fiber argument at that preimage gives a varying-effect curve.  Since \(\mathcal S\) is ambient open, it is Zariski dense, and because \(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal O_{3,3}\), it is also relatively Euclidean open in the legal image.  This proves nonidentification through order three.

For \(\ell=3\), the definitions give \(d_3=2\), \(h_3=1\), and \(U_3=4\).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:strict\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}and\mbox{-}recovery}\) supplies the nonempty order-four atlas, its relatively Zariski-open identifying union, its full-fiber ratio, and its failure convention.  Hence \(r_\beta(3)\le4\), while the order-three fiber curves give \(r_\beta(3)>3\).  Therefore \(r_\beta(3)=4\).  Finally
\[
 k(3)=5+\left\lceil\frac{-3+\sqrt{41}}2\right\rceil=7,
\]
which proves the stated reduction from seven to four and the order-three nonidentification conclusion.
